title: Dr. Padma Gurmet Conferred UT Ladakh State Award 2025 for Exemplary Service to Sowa-Rigpa Medicine
body_text:
Dr. Padma Gurmet, Director, National Institute of Sowa-Rigpa, Leh, has been conferred the UT Ladakh State Award for the year 2025 in recognition of his contribution to the preservation, promotion and development of the Sowa-Rigpa system of medicine in Ladakh.
The award was conferred by the Lieutenant Governor of Ladakh, Vinai Kumar Saxena, during the UT State Awards ceremony, where 36 distinguished individuals were honoured for the years 2022–2025 for their exceptional contributions and exemplary service in various fields.
Addressing the ceremony, the Lieutenant Governor highlighted that the awards are intended to recognise individuals whose dedication, excellence and service have made a meaningful impact on society. He also emphasised the importance of inspiring the younger generation to pursue excellence and contribute positively to the welfare and development of the Union Territory.
Dr. Padma Gurmet’s recognition is a matter of great pride for the National Institute of Sowa-Rigpa and represents an important acknowledgement of his sustained efforts towards the preservation, promotion and advancement of Sowa-Rigpa, one of Ladakh’s rich traditional systems of knowledge and healthcare.
The faculty, staff and students of the National Institute of Sowa-Rigpa, Leh, extended their heartfelt congratulations to Dr. Padma Gurmet on this prestigious honour and wished him continued success in his dedicated service towards the growth and development of Sowa-Rigpa.

enrichment.summary: Dr. Padma Gurmet, Director of the National Institute of Sowa-Rigpa (NISR), Leh, has been conferred the UT Ladakh State Award for 2025 for his contribution to preserving, promoting and developing the Sowa-Rigpa system of medicine. The award was presented by Lieutenant Governor Vinai Kumar Saxena at a ceremony honouring 36 individuals for the years 2022-2025 across various fields.
enrichment.context: Sowa-Rigpa, often called the 'Amchi' system of medicine, is a traditional healing system practiced predominantly in the Himalayan regions of India—Ladakh, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh, and parts of Himachal Pradesh—with roots shared with Tibetan medicine. It draws on Ayurvedic, Chinese and Tibetan medical traditions and uses natural herbs, minerals and dietary/lifestyle regulation for treatment. In 2010, the Government of India officially recognized Sowa-Rigpa under the Ministry of AYUSH (Ayurveda, Yoga & Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy), and the National Institute of Sowa-Rigpa in Leh was established to promote research, education and standardization of this system. This recognition is significant for the preservation of indigenous knowledge systems in India's border and high-altitude regions, aligning with broader government efforts to mainstream traditional and alternative medicine through AYUSH schemes such as the National AYUSH Mission. The UT Ladakh State Award itself reflects the administration's efforts, since Ladakh became a Union Territory in 2019, to recognize local achievers and preserve regional cultural and medical heritage.

prelims_questions.explanation: Sowa-Rigpa, also known as the Amchi system, is traditionally practiced in the Himalayan and high-altitude regions such as Ladakh, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh, and parts of Himachal Pradesh, and was officially recognized by the Government of India in 2010 under the Ministry of AYUSH.

prelims_questions.explanation: The National Institute of Sowa-Rigpa (NISR) is located in Leh, Union Territory of Ladakh, and works towards the promotion, research and standardization of the Sowa-Rigpa system of medicine.
